questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Porto-Novo?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Benin is Porto-Novo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Benin?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Benin on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Benin article.

questions.proof: Benin is bordered by Togo to the west, Burkina Faso and Niger to the north, Nigeria to the east, and the Bight of Benin to the south.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Benin about 114,763 square kilometres; Togo about 56,785 square kilometres; Equatorial Guinea about 28,051 square kilometres; São Tomé and Príncipe about 1,001 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Benin?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Benin article.

questions.proof: The capital of Benin is Porto-Novo.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Benin on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Benin on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
